| **PROS**    | **CONS**  |
|-------------------|-----------|
| 🟢 Incredible for surfing and rough water | 🟡 Feels slower than most boats |
| 🟢 Stellar in rocks | 🟡 Paddling with skeg is necessary |
| 🟢 Edging is outstanding | 🟡 More difficult to roll than other boats |

# Summary
The P&H Delphin 155 is fantastic for surfing and rough seas, handling itself well in rocky conditions where less robust models would struggle. Its edging is excellent, giving you accurate, quick control exactly when you need it. On the other hand, it does tend to feel slower than many other boats, so you will probably notice this over longer stretches of flat water. Due to the large amount of rocker, you'll likely need to paddle with the skeg partway down for nearly all trips. Moreover, it is harder to roll than other boats and therefore demands a high degree of skill and patience in this regard.

The bottom line with this boat is that it gives you massive confidence when paddling in rough waters. It just feels like it will do the right thing for you when a large wave washes you up a cliff face. For someone who values strong performance in difficult conditions over sheer speed, this boat is ideal. And, to be honest, once I paddled it for several months, the slower speed became less noticeable (maybe the boat makes you stronger too — bonus!).

# Buyer
Any paddler that loves rock gardening and surfing.
